answer: To prevent Sybil flooding, each validator must route traffic through a cryptographic inlet that checks hardware-level proofs from a trusted secure enclave. Identical replicas attempting to mimic distinct nodes get rejected at admission, forcing adversaries to purchase separate physical silicon chips. Because forging each identity demands burning a non-refundable bond locked in a marble vault, and acquiring dedicated ferrous sensor hardware scales linearly with node count, deploying a thousand fraudulent personas costs over $50,000 in physical capital.
